observations.observed: A prerequisite chain uses dim locked nodes and dashed links, activates successive connections, then compares this with radial choices around a shared endpoint. Bright active edges and node outlines lead attention.
observations.adopt: Progressive edge reveal, explicit state, preservation of object identity when explaining a different relationship.

observations.observed: A stylized race-car demonstration changes the apparent field of view, then cuts back to commercial gameplay. Other intervals compare blur/trails and camera viewpoints.
observations.adopt: Use a controlled demonstration of one variable and return to actual examples; renderer cannot be inferred from final pixels.

observations.observed: A visible reference line and cyan marker show a camera target moving ahead of a character. The forward space changes while the relation stays visible.
observations.adopt: Distinguish object anchor, camera/reference point and direction; animate the reason for a spatial change.

observations.observed: A main route and alternatives are separated by color/brightness; branches rejoin. A map image relates rewards to an overlaid path.
observations.adopt: Explain split→choice→merge with labeled roles, avoid treating route lines as measured player telemetry.
observations.limitation: Map video URL not supplied; only two stills were analyzed. Do not attribute exact movement/easing or tools.

observations.observed: The grid shows graphs, mathematical diagrams, stylized 3D demonstrations and commercial gameplay across topics.
observations.adopt: Select the renderer per concept, not a mandatory single-engine treatment.
observations.limitation: Grid thumbnails do not establish the tools used or animation behaviour.

toolAttribution.unity: Unconfirmed for these videos; visually compatible but not proof.
toolAttribution.motionCanvas: Unconfirmed; visual appearance alone cannot establish it.

confirmedCredits.descriptionCredit: 화살표 비디오 소스: Youtube channel freeticon

toolAttribution.ourImplementation: Unity is the user-selected default for self-authored game behavior and character animation demonstrations; Motion Canvas adds independently authored timed relationships and labels when useful. This is our production choice, not evidence of the reference creator's software.

batches.userRequest: 참고 영상 7편을 역으로 프레임 확인해 우리 영상 규칙에 반영; 기존 규칙은 유지/보강/변경을 판단해 수정. 기술 샘플은 뒤의 4편.

method.sceneChangeFrames: ffmpeg select gt(scene,0.25) per video (cuts: v0 114, v1 4, v2 3, v3 1, v4 41, v5 3, v6 4)
method.periodicSampling: 16:9 long videos every 4 s (v0 193, v3 146, v4 114 frames); vertical shorts every 1.5 s (v1 45, v2 33, v5 21, v6 37)
method.reviewed: Timestamped contact sheets of every periodic frame plus full-resolution zooms of definition cards, quote/number cards, on-scene numeric labels, recap grid, step-list chips and split A/B metric chips.
notClaimed: Audio listening or ASR of the reference narration
OCR; on-screen text transcribed by eye from 640x360 / 360x640 frames
Channel identity beyond the on-screen subscribe card text
Exact colors, fonts, easing or timing of the reference
method.filesLocation: User Downloads folder; not copied into the repository under the media policy
method.denseSampling: v0 first short (0-80 s) at 1 fps for beat timing; v0/v1/v2 full-resolution zooms of reveal stamp, game-name chips, measurement callouts, mannequin diagrams, split netcode view, formula card, debug-view footage.

sources.contentSummary: Mascot-boy channel compilation: destruction decals, long hair cards/strand hair, fake window interiors (interior mapping), high heels and skeleton height, oversized doors, SNES tilemap affine tricks, mirrors (duplicate room / SSR), delay vs rollback netcode, lag compensation, camera lerp/dead zone, coyote time, corner correction, hitboxes. Top title with yellow keyword, white outlined captions, source game name chips, 2D vector diagrams, recommended-video end card.

Billboarding in 3D games: 2D sprites facing the camera (pixel sprites, Super Mario 64 trees/enemies with red boxes), view-plane-aligned vs viewpoint-oriented wireframe diagrams, particle effects, grass/tree billboards rotating around the vertical axis only.
Normal maps: flat lit tiles with light direction arrows, normal map image, per-pixel direction storage, Dead Cells sprite-based normal map workflow, 3D wall with/without normal mapping.

Anti-cheat architecture on one low-poly PC model in a dark grid space: client/server authority, kernel, kernel anti-cheat and signed-driver holes, secure boot, TPM hash chain, remote attestation, DMA cards and IOMMU, input analysis, honeypots, replay analysis, ban waves, driver certificates, scale metaphor. Persistent top-left term chip, definition cards, primary-source quote cards, big-number cards, flow/state diagrams, timeline bars, continuous camera (one hard cut in 9m43s).

Game lighting history on ONE alley test-bed scene (Unreal-engine labelled): single ambient number, lightmap baking with a numeric example, dynamic light with per-light dot values, shadow volume, shadow map with depth comparison in meters, cascaded shadow maps, deferred G-buffers, SSAO, SSR, light propagation volumes, ray tracing, BVH, hybrid, ray-traced GI, path tracing, denoising, frame accumulation, 2x2 recap grid. Top-left term chip with engine/source sub-line and era, top-right current-picture line, on-scene numbers, log-scale time bars, film/game timeline.

Smart-object style NPC behaviour in a voxel life-sim scene: top claim headline, object-attached step list chip with the current step highlighted, hunger bar label, NPC-side code step chip, many objects each carrying their own usage steps.

Enemy slot system: slot ring around the player with state-coloured dots, queueing behind occupied slots, wall-blocked slots, top/bottom split A/B (single target vs slot row) with measured chips, formation matching nearest-first vs sorted vs Hungarian with total distances labelled as from the creator's own rig.

observations.observed: Opens on the low-poly PC model with the cheat problem already visible; the camera glides along the mouse cable while glowing dots travel the wire; labels name GPU, mouse device and kernel layers on the model.
observations.adopt: One system model, camera moves to the discussed part, data flow as moving dots along a path.

observations.observed: Definition card top-left: small caps CLIENT, bold 클라이언트, plain meaning 플레이어 PC에서 도는 게임; it then collapses into a small persistent chip for the chapter. A separate source chip (company · products · date) appears under it before quotes.
observations.adopt: Term definition card that collapses into a persistent term chip; canonical KO/EN at first appearance.

observations.observed: Quote card: English original with the key phrase highlighted, Korean translation, source line (team · date · document). The caption below keeps one clause with one coloured keyword.
observations.adopt: Primary-source quote card type; captions one clause, one emphasis.

observations.observed: Big-number card 약 3분의 1 with a dot pictogram (coloured subset of a grid) and legend chip; later 34.33%, 약 26만 건, 100만 달러 with a one-line context and source line.
observations.adopt: Number card type with pictogram and source line; keep 약.

observations.observed: Boot-chain flow boxes (펌웨어→부트로더→운영체제) with sub-lines; a red cheat badge inserted between nodes; secure-boot question/answer badges; hash chain table with red mismatched values.
observations.adopt: Flow/state diagram with status badges; red = compromised, cyan = verified, always with text labels.

observations.observed: Timeline bar PC 켬 → 게임 켬 → 시간 with driver bars appearing before/after the anti-cheat; checklist of required protections; diagrams fade in while the 3D world stays dimmed behind.
observations.adopt: Timeline bars for ordering claims; the world stays dimmed behind cards.

observations.observed: Ends by returning to the full PC model with all layer labels and a game-server icon: the opening model now annotated with everything taught.
observations.adopt: Close on the same model/scene with the accumulated labels.

observations.observed: First frames show the finished ray-traced alley with the character, caption 빛을 레이로 계산해요, then rewinds to 숫자 하나였어요 and the history begins on the same alley.
observations.adopt: Overview over the hero scene with the end result visible, then rewind.

observations.observed: Lightmap numeric example on the floor grid: 96, −16, 152, +16, 168 appear one term at a time while the caption says 한 단계씩만 고쳐요.
observations.adopt: Small worked example on the scene, one term at a time.

observations.observed: Per-light values on the live scene: 조명 1 · 면이 이 빛을 보는 정도 0.84, 조명 2 · 0.97, 조명마다 계산해서 더한다, with a leader line from the surface to the light.
observations.adopt: On-scene numbers with leader lines; role colours per value.

observations.observed: Shadow-map comparison labels top-right: 섀도 맵에 적힌 깊이 4.2 m (cyan), 이 픽셀에서 조명까지 5.4 m (orange), 더 멀다 = 그늘. Chip reads 새도 맵 · 1978년에 나온 방법.
observations.adopt: Depth/comparison labels with units and a conclusion; era in the term chip.

observations.observed: Top-right line 화면으로 흉내 marks an imitated effect; later chips read 언리얼 엔진의 버퍼, 우리가 빛을 뭉갠 그림, (우리 계산).
observations.adopt: Current-picture label distinguishing engine output, our drawing and imitation.

observations.observed: The same alley re-rendered as CSM distance colouring, deferred G-buffer panels (depth/normal/colour), SSAO grey pass, SSR, LPV voxel grid, ray lines, BVH boxes, path-tracing noise, denoise tile, always with the same framing.
observations.adopt: One test-bed scene across all techniques; only the technique changes.

observations.observed: Log-scale time bar card: 미리 베이크 · 둠 이터널의 큰 맵 하나 40시간 (red) vs 게임 중에 · 프레임마다의 간접광 약 2 ms (green) on a 1 ms … 100시간 axis, source id Software 의 발표.
observations.adopt: Log-scale cost bar card with unit ticks and a source line.

observations.observed: Film vs game timeline (1995 Toy Story, 2004 Doom 3, 2018 RTX, 2023 Cyberpunk) as two tracks on one year axis.
observations.adopt: Two-track timeline card.

observations.observed: Recap: side-by-side 1996년 베이킹 도구 vs 지금 게임, then a 2x2 grid (숫자 하나 / 라이트맵 / 레이트레이싱 / 패스 트레이싱) of the same alley.
observations.adopt: Same-scene comparison grid as the closing summary.

observations.observed: Fixed top headline 주민은 냉장고 쓰는 법을 모릅니다 with the keyword in yellow; square footage in the middle; captions of 2–4 words on the black band below; a step-list chip attached to the fridge (슬롯으로 이동 / 문 열고 꺼내기 / 배고픔 채우기) with the current step highlighted and a hunger-bar label on the NPC.
observations.adopt: Shorts headline band, object-attached step list with current-step highlight.

observations.observed: NPC-side step chip (고르기 / 걸어가기 / 목록 실행) next to the character; later every object carries its own list, and a contrast chip lists what the NPC would need if it held all the logic.
observations.adopt: Two-sided responsibility chips; contrast card at the end.

observations.observed: Slot ring around the player drawn as dots: green empty, yellow reserved/target, red occupied; enemies queue behind full slots; wall-blocked slots and a counter 커진 슬롯 8 → 4.
observations.adopt: State-coloured slot dots with labels; counters for one-variable changes.

observations.observed: Top/bottom split A/B on the same scene: 한 점 표적 (red) vs 슬롯 한 줄 (green) with metric chips 표적에 닿은 적 8 / 서로 미는 양 23.5 m/s vs 9 / 0.7 m/s, and a small 우리 리그 tag.
observations.adopt: Same-position split A/B with measured chips from our own implementation, labelled as such.

observations.observed: Formation matching: lines from units to slots, pair counts 엇갈린 쌍 16 vs 4, total distances 가까운 순 61.1 / 정렬 56.3 / 헝가리안 56.0 m with 우리 리그.
observations.adopt: Progressive assignment lines and a totals chip; measured values only from our rig.

observations.observed: One short measured at 1 fps: 0-4 s real game (Battlefield 4 chip) with mascot pointing; 2 s big 가짜! stamp + mascot X sign; 5-6 s film meme; 7-17 s diagram (intact square -> pre-drawn cracks -> swap, shatter); 18-23 s Battlefield Bad Company confirming 'always the same collapse'; 24-34 s diagram of impact stickers then '이런 불박이 스티커를 데칼이라고 합니다'; 35-41 s Donkey Kong Bananza (green circle) decal growing and breaking; 42-45 s pre-split pieces diagram; 46-49 s Control; 50-54 s real-time slicing diagram; 55-60 s The Finals; 61-67 s node/link stress diagram; 68-73 s The Finals debug view; 74-78 s Rainbow Six Siege X + mascot '…파괴 연출을 제작한다고 하네요'. Roughly 38 s real game vs 40 s diagram, alternating every 5-10 s, five games across genres incl. one Nintendo title, each used for one claim.
observations.adopt: Phenomenon -> reveal -> principle diagram -> real-game confirmation -> naming after the mechanism -> cross-genre variants -> depth -> closing with the developer's actual choice; strict diagram/game alternation; one game per claim.

observations.observed: Long-hair short: TLOU2 (green circle on short hair) -> Animal Crossing hair UI -> hair-card diagram on a platform -> joints on cards -> red circle on clipping bug with mascot X -> strand hair -> Pragmata '2만 가닥' -> red circle on stiff cards -> CEDEC slide -> Resident Evil -> '게임사들은 단발 캐릭터를 선택한다고 하네요'.
observations.adopt: Green circle = look here, red circle = problem; closing names the studios' real decision.

observations.observed: Fake window interiors: Pokemon Legends Z-A window -> Spider-Man -> unfolded cube-map room diagram -> 'interior mapping' named after showing -> Spider-Man window (green circle) -> building grid with camera ray diagram computing which cell to draw.
observations.adopt: Player view vs actual structure; name the technique after the mechanism.

observations.observed: High heels: Saints Row shoe menu (red circle) -> white articulated mannequin with height arrow -> red heels -> chair -> door -> GTA V (green circle) -> capsule diagram 'hit range changes' -> two mannequins compared -> Cyberpunk/Witcher shoe UIs -> Sims 4.
observations.adopt: Neutral articulated mannequin + minimal props; one cause (height) followed through several props.

observations.observed: Door size: Gears of War door -> mannequin + door 'too small -> hard with controller' -> Rainbow Six door with measurement '213 cm / ??? cm' and green circle -> FOV reasoning -> Halo Infinite -> stairs -> Digimon rooms.
observations.adopt: Measured values only where known; unknown shown as ?, never invented.

observations.observed: SNES tricks: tilemap -> affine formulas x'=1.5x, y'=2y, shear tan30 with small grid -> Super Mario Kart -> Chrono Trigger -> CRT scanline diagram drawing line by line -> per-line rotation -> Mario Kart.
observations.adopt: Small formula cards next to the diagram; math beats stay short.

observations.observed: Mirrors: Doom 3 가짜! -> duplicate room diagram -> Mario 64 mirror -> Doom 3 -> cube-map photo and vase -> UE editor distortion -> SSR ray-to-screen diagram -> neon city scene -> Cyberpunk puddle.
observations.adopt: Reveal first, then two alternative techniques each confirmed by a game.

observations.observed: Netcode: two side-by-side screens (blue frame = my screen, red frame = opponent) with pixel fighters, packet arrow animation, 'delay netcode' vs 'rollback netcode', USF4 and SF6 clips.
observations.adopt: Same-time side-by-side views with one variable (latency) and labelled frames.

observations.observed: Lag compensation: mascot shooting diagram with server icon, a 시점 timeline (나/상대/서버 chips), ghost silhouettes for past positions, yellow shot trace, 과거…현재 bar; CS2 clips; cat GIF meme; '사람들은 납득하고 넘어간다고 하네요'.
observations.adopt: Timeline bar + ghost positions for time-rewind explanations; memes not adopted (cat reaction instead).

observations.observed: Camera math: minimal city silhouette, character and camera icon, graph with x_{t+1}=x_t+0.1(target-x_t) converging curve, '점근적 평균', dead-zone dashed lines.
observations.adopt: Graph + formula card beside the moving object (Manim).

observations.observed: Coyote time / corner correction: pixel pig on platforms, orange circle at the ledge, panda GIF, Road Runner cartoon, green trajectory arrows vs red blocked line, Super Mario Bros, wall jump, moving platform, Celeste.
observations.adopt: Trajectory arrows green = allowed path, red = blocked; one-variable jump comparisons.

observations.observed: Hitboxes: sawblade + pixel knight, green/red boxes, live-action fighter clip, monster hitbox, Geometry Dash, hit-stop, Hollow Knight debug boxes; end card '추천 영상 / 구독하기' with mascot.
observations.adopt: Hit/hurt boxes as labelled editorial guides; official debug views only from independently obtained footage.

observations.observed: Vertical short: self-made pixel-sprite 3D scene -> side-by-side 'view plane aligned | viewpoint oriented' wireframes with the camera frustum -> Super Mario 64 (red boxes on trees/enemies) -> '빌보드라고 합니다' -> particles/Dragon Quest -> clouds and trees rotating about the vertical axis -> modern games.
observations.adopt: Player view | outside structure split; Unity 2D sprites for self-made demo scenes.

observations.observed: Normal maps: pixel knight scene 'light moves but graphics flat' -> tiles with light-direction arrows -> normal-map image -> per-pixel direction -> sprite with/without -> Dead Cells workflow -> 3D wall with/without normal map -> game footage.
observations.adopt: Before/after with one condition in the same framing.

notAdopted: Dark-navy background and pastel low-poly palette (keep research-black-v1)
Subscribe pill, channel name, logo glyph, mascot characters
On-screen source lines under footage (ours go to the description bottom)
No-branding cold open (keep the 2 s branding)
batches.openDecisionForUser: The technical samples are almost entirely self-authored engine scenes; under current contracts self-authored Unity test beds count as explanation footage, so a v4-style video would need an explicit per-video ratio exception.

contentGrammar.appliesTo: game-design longform chapters (Sakurai-referenced structure kept) and game-content shorts
notAdopted: Mascot boy, 가짜! stamp artwork, outlined captions
Film scenes, meme GIFs and live-action clips
